stm32-an2586-p0008-figure-00003.luna:
**Figure 3. Power on reset/power down reset waveform**

- The figure shows the relationship between the supply voltage **VDD** and the **RESET** signal during power-on and power-down.
- Vertical axis: **VDD** (arrow upward).
- Horizontal axis: time progression (arrow to the right; no axis label visible).

**VDD waveform and thresholds**
- VDD starts near zero, ramps upward, reaches a high-level plateau, then ramps downward back toward zero.
- Two horizontal dashed threshold lines are shown.
- The voltage difference between the thresholds is labeled **“40 mV hysteresis”**, with a vertical double-headed arrow.
- **POR** is labeled at the rising-voltage threshold region.
- **PDR** is labeled at the falling-voltage threshold region.
- Dashed vertical timing markers extend from the relevant threshold crossings toward the RESET waveform.

**RESET waveform**
- **RESET** is labeled at the left.
- RESET is initially low.
- During VDD ramp-up, RESET remains low until the reset-release timing interval expires, then transitions high.
- RESET remains high while VDD is at its operating plateau.
- During VDD ramp-down, RESET transitions low at the power-down reset threshold and remains low.

**Timing annotation**
- The interval between the rising-threshold crossing and RESET release is shown with a horizontal double-headed arrow labeled:
  - **Temporization**
  - **tRSTTEMPO**

- Figure identifier at lower right: **ai14364**.

stm32-an2586-p0009-figure-00004.luna:
**Figure 4. PVD thresholds** (source: STM32 AN2586, p. 9)

- Upper graph shows the supply voltage **VDD** versus time:
  - Vertical axis is labeled **VDD** with an upward arrow.
  - Horizontal time axis is drawn with a right-pointing arrow but has no visible label.
  - VDD starts at the baseline, rises linearly, reaches a flat plateau, remains constant, then falls linearly back to the baseline.
  - Two horizontal dashed lines indicate the PVD threshold levels.
  - The region between the dashed levels is labeled **PVD threshold**.
  - A vertical double-headed arrow at the right identifies the separation between the two levels as **100 mV hysteresis**.
  - Dashed vertical guide lines mark the rising-voltage crossing of the upper threshold and the falling-voltage crossing of the lower threshold.

- Lower graph shows **PVD output**:
  - Label: **PVD output**.
  - The output is at a high level before the rising-threshold crossing.
  - It transitions downward at the left dashed vertical guide and remains low while VDD is between the threshold crossings.
  - It transitions upward at the right dashed vertical guide and returns to the high level.
  - The waveform has no numerical voltage scale or explicit logic-high/logic-low labels.

- Figure identifier at bottom right: **ai14365**.

stm32-an2586-p0010-figure-00005.luna:
**Figure 5. Reset circuit** (source: STM32 AN2586, p. 10; figure identifier: **ai14366c**)

- Left side: dashed-outline **External reset circuit** connected to the **NRST** node.
  - The external circuit shows a push-button/switch symbol connected to ground.
  - A capacitor labeled **0.1 μF** is also connected from the NRST line to ground.
- The NRST input is shown entering a device/input block labeled **NRST**.
- NRST has an internal pull-up resistor labeled **RPU**, connected to **VDD/VDDA**.
- The NRST node also connects to a pull-down/reset transistor symbol connected to ground.
- The NRST signal passes through a buffer/input symbol and then into a block labeled **Filter**.
- The filter output is labeled **System reset**.
- A branch from the reset circuitry feeds a block labeled **Pulse generator (min 20 μs)**.
- The pulse-generator output enters a multi-input reset-combining gate. Its labeled reset sources are:
  - **WWDG reset**
  - **IWDG reset**
  - **Power reset**
  - **Software reset**
  - **Low-power management reset**
- The diagram explicitly labels the supply connection as **VDD/VDDA** and the pull-up resistor as **RPU**.

stm32-an2586-p0024-figure-00012.luna:
**Figure 14. STM32F103ZE(T6) microcontroller reference schematic**

The figure is a reference schematic for an **STM32F103ZE(T6)** MCU, showing power/VBAT connections, decoupling capacitors, JTAG, boot-mode selection, high- and low-speed oscillators, and reset circuitry.

### MCU and GPIO labels

The main MCU symbol is labeled **STM32F103ZE(T6)** / **MCU**. The visible GPIO groups are:

- **PA0–PA15**
- **PB0–PB15**
- **PC0–PC15**
- **PD0–PD15**
- **PE0–PE15**
- **PF0–PF15**
- **PG0–PG15**

The symbol also shows the supply/control labels:

- **VDD**
- **VSS**
- **VDDA**
- **VSSA**
- **VREF+**
- **VREF−**
- **VBAT**
- **BOOT0**
- **NRST**
- **OSC_IN**
- **OSC_OUT**
- **OSC32_IN**
- **OSC32_OUT**

The small pin numbers around the MCU are shown in the schematic; many of the individual numbers are too small to transcribe reliably from the crop.

### Power supply and VBAT section

The upper-left section, marked **MCU Supply**, connects the MCU supply pins to **VDD** and ground. It includes:

- Multiple **100 nF** bypass capacitors from VDD to ground.
- MCU pins labeled **VDD**, **VSS**, **VDDA**, **VSSA**, **VREF+**, **VREF−**, and **VBAT**.
- A battery symbol labeled **BT1** with battery type **CR1220**.
- A jumper/selection connection near the battery with the note **Default setting 2-3**.
- VDD and ground power symbols.

### Decoupling capacitors

The right-hand vertical bank is labeled **Decoupling Capacitor**. It contains capacitors:

- **C6 — 100 nF**
- **C7 — 100 nF**
- **C8 — 100 nF**
- **C9 — 100 nF**
- **C10 — 100 nF**
- **C11 — 100 nF**
- **C12 — 100 nF**
- **C13 — 100 nF**
- **C14 — 100 nF**
- **C15 — 100 nF**
- **C16 — 100 nF**
- **C17 — 100 nF**

The capacitors are connected between the **VDD** rail and ground.

### JTAG connector

The lower-left section is labeled **JTAG connector** and uses connector **CN1**, marked **JTAG**. The connector is numbered **1 through 20** and is wired to MCU debug/JTAG-related signals and ground/power connections.

The visible JTAG-related MCU signals include:

- **JTMS/SWDIO**
- **JTCK/SWCLK**
- **JTDI**
- **JTDO**
- **NJTRST**
- **NRST**

Pull/resistor components visible in this area include:

- **R1 — 10K**
- **R2 — 10K**
- **R3 — 10K**
- **R4 — 10K**

The exact function of every CN1 numbered contact is not legible at the crop resolution, although all connector numbers 1–20 are visible.

### Boot-mode selection

Two separate boot-selection circuits are shown:

#### Boot 1

The circuit is labeled **Boot Mode** and **Boot1**. It includes:

- **SW1**
- A **VDD** connection
- A ground connection
- **R4 — 10K**
- Connection to the MCU **BOOT1** signal, associated with **PB2**.

#### Boot 0

The circuit is labeled **Boot Mode** and **Boot0**. It includes:

- **SW2**
- A **VDD** connection
- A ground connection
- A **10K** pull resistor
- Connection to the MCU **BOOT0** pin.

### High-speed external oscillator

The center-right oscillator section is labeled **HSE**. It connects to:

- **OSC_IN**
- **OSC_OUT**
- Crystal **Y1**, labeled **8 MHz**
- **C3 — 20 pF**
- **C4 — 20 pF**

C3 and C4 are connected from the oscillator nodes to ground.

### Low-speed external oscillator

The nearby section is labeled **LSE**. It connects to:

- **OSC32_IN**
- **OSC32_OUT**
- Crystal **Y2**, labeled **32.768 kHz**
- **C1 — 10 pF**
- **C2 — 10 pF**

C1 and C2 are connected from the low-speed oscillator nodes to ground.

### Reset circuit

The lower-right section is labeled **Reset** and connects to the MCU **NRST** pin. It contains:

- **R5 — 330** (the value is printed as “330” in the crop)
- **C5 — 100 nF**
- Pushbutton **B1**
- A VDD connection through the resistor
- A ground connection through the reset switch/capacitor network

The MCU reset pin is labeled **NRST**, with the visible package pin number **25** adjacent to it.
